messages:
maria: Heads-up — last-night spot churn spiked tail latency for tier-B customers, ~18% p95 increase. Proposing a 'tiered eject + staggered fanout' pattern: quick local warm fallback, short retry window, then staged regional fanout, then model-variant degrade. Sketch below, want quick feedback before we test in us-west. @devon @lucy

devon: Can you post the numbers / which pools were evicted?

maria: p50 stable; p95 jumped 210ms -> 340ms. Evictions were concentrated on A100 spot pools in us-west1 (multiple preemptions). Affected serving variants: sft-small, sft-medium. Dedicated and reserved pools unaffected.

lucy: I agree we should avoid immediate full-region fanout — that nukes KV/prefix cache hit rates and makes things worse. Staggered fanout + small-quantized variant fallback is the least-bad path. :thinking:

kai: Proposal: make routing SLO-aware per-tenant. If tier=enterprise -> route to dedicated/warm-reserve. If tier=B -> allow 2 retries in-zone (fast), then start staggered fanout to up to 3 regions with exponential backoff.

chetan: We'll need a small config shape. Rough draft:

```json
"eject_policy": {
  "initial_retry_ms": 50,
  "max_retries": 2,
  "local_warm_fallback": true,
  "regional_fanout_after_ms": 250,
  "regional_fanout_stagger_ms": 120,
  "variant_fallback_pct": 0.2,
  "max_fanout_nodes": 3
}
```

ops-bot: incident: spot-eviction-spike detected 2026-02-14T03:12Z — 42 preemptions in 15m in us-west1 (auto-alert).

maria: Important details: variant_fallback_pct is the fraction of requests we route to quantized/low-rank variant to protect latency while keeping quality sampling for monitoring. We must gate that by evals.

devon: Concern: 0.2 might introduce user-visible quality regressions. We need a quick eval harness and a canary flag that requires quality-drop < 0.3% on known prompt set before increasing pct. Also prefer A/B controlled rollouts.

lucy: Add metric and alert: "variant_quality_drop" and auto-rollback if >0.5% over a 5m window. Also emit per-tenant quality metrics so we don't hide small enterprise regressions.

kai: Also add a soft cross-region throttler to limit fanout bursts — token_bucket with 200 qps/burst per-region so fanout doesn't saturate egress or remote caches.

maria: Plan: I'll open PR with config + sim results for us-west tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Quick tests: latency sim shows p95 improvement vs naive fanout, cost delta ~+6% for tier-B but avoids 3x transient latency spikes. Link to sim: https://redwood.internal/sim/fanout-2026-02-14

chetan: If we go live, update runbook: add step to prewarm a tiny dedicated warm-reserve for tier-A and enterprise customers (failover target). Also include a manual kill-switch to disable fanout.

lucy: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary scheduled for config change: 2026-02-15T09:00UTC -> us-west1 (canary). Rollout policy: 10% nodes -> 30m -> 50% -> monitor.

maria: Thanks all — will PR and include gating eval, metric alerts, and runbook updates. We should keep the config conservative for the first week and monitor cost/quality.

devon: Great. One more ask: add histogram of cache-hit-rate pre/post fanout so we can correlate latency changes.

maria: Will add that to the dashboard query.

ops-bot: reminder: add pager schedule for on-call during canary window (2026-02-15 09:00-12:00 UTC).

maria: Done. Thanks everyone.
